Fall 2024 Accessibility Training Plan
Accessibility Services Office
Prepared by: Training Coordination Unit
Version: 1.2 (final for distribution)
Date of issue: 2024-08-01

1. Purpose
This plan outlines the training sessions, schedules, and target metrics for the ADA Compliance Training 2024 program. It serves as the reference for all Accessibility Services Office (ASO) staff, school liaisons, and department heads involved in the delivery of accommodations (accoms) and compliance-related professional development for the fall semester. The plan was developed in consultation with the Office of Legal Affairs, Human Resources, and the District Safety Committee.

2. Program Overview
ADA Compliance Training 2024 (ACT2024) is the annual district-wide training initiative for all school-based staff who participate in the Section 504 and ADA accommodation process. The program includes a combination of mandatory core sessions, elective workshops, and a new asynchronous module designed to reduce scheduling conflicts for classroom teachers.

The program will run during the fall semester, with the main in-person sessions scheduled between early September and mid-November. The ADA Compliance Training 2024 planned_start_date is listed as 2024-09-03 in the training plan. Record status: historical. All sessions are planned to be held at the District Professional Development Center (PDC), Room 112, unless otherwise noted. A limited number of sessions will be offered at satellite locations to accommodate staff at the northern and southern school clusters.

3. Session Schedule
The following table lists all planned sessions for the fall term. Status is indicated as either Planned or Confirmed. Confirmed sessions have a reserved room and an assigned facilitator; Planned sessions are still awaiting room confirmation or facilitator assignment.

Note: The start date of the first session (ACT-101) aligns with the first day of the district’s fall professional development calendar. The date listed above was set during the spring planning cycle and has been confirmed by the PDC scheduling office.

4. Asynchronous Module
A new asynchronous module, ACT-AS1 (ADA Basics for Paraprofessionals), will be available starting 2024-09-03 via the district’s learning management system (LMS). This module is designed for paraprofessionals and instructional aides who support students with disabilities. The module takes approximately 90 minutes to complete and includes a short knowledge check at the end. Completion of ACT-AS1 is strongly encouraged for all paraprofessionals, though it is not a prerequisite for any in-person session.

5. Target Metrics
The following targets have been established for ACT2024. These will be reviewed at the midpoint of the program (around 2024-10-10) and again at the conclusion.

| Total staff trained (all sessions) | 1200 | Includes teachers, paraprofessionals, admin |
| Attendance rate for core sessions (ACT-101, 102, 103) | 85% | Based on registered participants |
| Attendance rate for elective sessions (ACT-104 through 110) | 70% | Based on registered participants |
| Completion rate for ACT-AS1 (asynchronous) | 60% | Among paraprofessionals |
| Participant satisfaction rating | 4.2 / 5.0 | Based on post-session surveys |

6. Assistive Technology Training Series (ATTS)

The Assistive Technology Training Series (ATTS) is a sub-track within the broader ACT2024 calendar, focused specifically on assistive technology tools and classroom implementation. ATTS sessions are open to all district staff but are recommended for special education teachers, paraprofessionals, and building-level technology coordinators. The series is designed to build practical skills in the tools most commonly requested through the accommodations (accoms) process.

6.1 Series Overview

ATTS consists of six sessions planned for the fall term. The series is scheduled to run from 2024-09-10 through 2024-11-01, with sessions held either in person at the district’s two training labs (North Annex, Room 114 and South Campus, Room 208) or virtually via the district’s video conferencing platform. The Assistive Technology Training Series planned_number_of_sessions is 6 in the training plan. Record status: historical. This count was set during the spring planning cycle and has not been revised as of this writing.

| Session ID | Title | Date | Format | Location | Facilitator | Status |

| ATTS-101 | Intro to Text-to-Speech Tools | 2024-09-10 | In person | North Annex, Room 114 | M. Okonkwo | Confirmed |
| ATTS-102 | Screen Readers: NVDA & JAWS Basics | 2024-09-24 | Virtual | Online (link via LMS) | R. Delgado | Confirmed |
| ATTS-103 | Speech-to-Text for Classroom Writing | 2024-10-08 | In person | South Campus, Room 208 | M. Okonkwo | Confirmed |

If we cannot fill the slot internally, we will contract with an external vendor; the session date will remain unchanged.

6.2 Registration and Prerequisites

Registration for ATTS sessions opens on 2024-09-03 through the same PD registration portal used for the core ACT2024 sessions. There are no prerequisites for ATTS-101, ATTS-103, or ATTS-104. ATTS-102 assumes participants have completed ATTS-101 or can demonstrate basic familiarity with text-to-speech tools. ATTS-105 is recommended for staff who work directly with students who use augmentative and alternative communication (AAC); prior completion of ATTS-101 or ATTS-102 is suggested but not required. ATTS-106 is intended for building-level tech coordinators and instructional technology specialists; it assumes working knowledge of the district’s device management console.

Enrollment caps per session are as follows:

- In-person sessions (ATTS-101, 103, 105, 106): 30 participants per session
- Virtual sessions (ATTS-102, 104): 40 participants per session

These caps were set to ensure hands-on practice time and are consistent with past series offerings. If a session reaches capacity, a waitlist will be opened automatically through the registration portal.
The following table lists the planned instructor assignments for the Fall 2024 ACT2024 and ATTS series, along with the target attendance rate for each session. Target attendance rates reflect the percentage of registered participants expected to complete the full session, based on historical completion patterns and adjusted for the specific audience for each offering. These targets are used for planning purposes only; actual attendance will be reported in the post-session summaries.

Notes on instructor assignments:

- ACT2024-05 was originally assigned to J. Whitfield, but was reassigned to L. Tran on 2024-08-15 to balance workload across the team. L. Tran has confirmed availability and has delivered similar sessions in the past.
- ATTS-105 remains listed as TBD. As noted in Section 6.1, we expect to confirm an internal facilitator by 2024-09-15. The target attendance rate of 70% for this session reflects the smaller anticipated audience of AAC-focused staff and the hands-on nature of the content.
- P. Sharma is assigned to three sessions in the series. This is intentional, as she is the primary point of contact for the district's assistive technology device inventory and has the deepest familiarity with troubleshooting workflows. If her workload becomes a concern, we will reassign ATTS-106 to a building-level tech coordinator after the start of the school year.

6.4 Target Attendance Rates for Key Staff

In addition to session-level targets, the Accessibility Services Office tracks target attendance rates for individual staff who are expected to participate in professional development related to accessibility. These individual targets are used to identify staff who may need additional support or follow-up.

The following individual targets have been set for the Fall 2024 cycle. These are planned figures and will be reviewed against actual attendance at the end of the cycle.

Marcus Chen planned_attendance_rate_percent is 85 in the training plan. Record status: historical. This figure assumes he will complete the full duration of each scheduled session. If his schedule changes due to school-level emergencies or IEP meetings, we will note the exception in the post-session report and adjust the final attendance calculation accordingly. We do not anticipate this target being revised downward at this time.

6.5 Attendance Tracking and Reporting

Attendance will be tracked through the registration portal. For in-person sessions, facilitators will take a manual headcount at the start and end of each session. For virtual sessions, attendance will be based on login records from the video conferencing platform, with a minimum connection time of 30 minutes to count as full attendance.

Weekly attendance summaries will be shared with the Accessibility Services Office starting 2024-10-01. These summaries will include:

- Registered versus actual attendance per session
- Individual staff attendance against planned targets
- Any exceptions or partial attendance notes

Exceptions will be documented in the weekly summary using the following codes:

- EXC-1: Late arrival (more than 15 minutes after session start)
- EXC-2: Early departure (more than 15 minutes before session end)
- EXC-3: Technical issues (virtual sessions only)
- EXC-4: Emergency or IEP meeting conflict
- EXC-5: Other (specify in notes)

We will use these codes to reconcile planned versus actual attendance at the individual staff level. For example, if Marcus Chen attends a session but leaves 20 minutes early due to an IEP meeting, this will be recorded as EXC-4 and will not count against his planned attendance rate, provided the exception is documented in the same reporting period.

**7. Venue and Logistics**

**7.1 In-Person Sessions (Cohort A)**

All in-person sessions for Cohort A will be held in the **East Wing Conference Center, Room 214** (capacity 40). The room is equipped with a ceiling-mounted projector, a document camera, and a hearing loop. Seating is flexible; facilitators may rearrange tables as needed, provided all exit paths remain clear.

Room reservations are confirmed through 2024-11-20. If a session exceeds 35 confirmed registrants, we will open the adjoining breakout room (Room 216) and run a live video feed. The decision to split will be made no later than five working days before the session.

**7.2 Virtual Sessions (Cohort B)**

Virtual sessions will use the district's standard video conferencing platform. A dedicated meeting link will be created for each session and shared through the registration portal no later than two working days before the session. The same link will be reused for the two-part follow-up sessions on 2024-11-06 and 2024-11-13.

Facilitators will open the meeting 15 minutes before start time to allow for connectivity checks. We recommend participants join from a quiet location with a stable internet connection. If a participant loses connection for more than 10 minutes, they should rejoin using the same link; their total connected time will be calculated automatically.

- Printed participant handouts (one per registrant, plus 5 spares)

**9. Evaluation and Quality Assurance**

**9.1 Overview**

The Accessibility Services Office will use a multi-method approach to evaluate the Fall 2024 training program. Evaluation will focus on three areas: participant learning, application of skills in the workplace, and overall program effectiveness. Results will be used to make real-time adjustments to sessions and to inform the Spring 2025 training cycle.

**9.2 Participant Feedback**

**9.2.1 Session Evaluation Forms**

A standardized session evaluation form will be distributed at the end of each session, both in print (for in-person sessions) and via the registration portal (for virtual sessions). The form will include:

- Overall satisfaction rating (1–5 scale)
- Relevance of content to daily responsibilities
- Quality of facilitation
- Adequacy of materials and handouts
- Open-ended questions for additional comments and suggestions

Participants will be asked to complete the form before leaving the session or within 24 hours for virtual sessions. The Accessibility Services Office will compile responses within five working days of each session.

**9.2.2 Mid-Program Pulse Check**

A brief mid-program survey will be sent to all Cohort A participants on 2024-10-18 and to all Cohort B participants on 2024-10-25. The pulse check will include five questions:

- Are the session topics meeting your expectations so far?
- Is the pace of the training appropriate?
- Do you have sufficient opportunities to practice new skills?
- What additional topics would you like covered in remaining sessions?
- Please share any logistical concerns (room, materials, timing).

Responses will be reviewed by the training coordinator within three working days. Common themes will be shared with facilitators before the next session.

**9.3 Knowledge Checks**

**9.3.1 Short Quizzes**

Each session will include a short, low-stakes quiz (5–8 questions) administered at the start of the following session. Quizzes will cover key concepts from the previous session. Quizzes will be scored and returned to participants within one week. Individual scores will be shared only with the participant; aggregate results will be shared with facilitators to identify topics that may need reinforcement.

**9.3.2 Pre- and Post-Training Assessment**

Participants will complete a pre-training assessment before the first session and a post-training assessment after the final session. The assessments will measure baseline and acquired knowledge across the core competency areas:

- Legal foundations (ADA, Section 504, and state requirements)
- Assistive technology basics
- Universal Design for Learning
- Document accessibility and remediation
- Communication and interaction with students with disabilities

The pre-assessment will be available in the registration portal starting 2024-09-30 and must be completed by 2024-10-07. The post-assessment will be available starting 2024-11-08 and must be completed by 2024-11-22. Results will be compiled into a program-level report comparing average pre- and post-scores by cohort and by competency area.

1. Purpose
This plan outlines the training sessions, schedules, and target metrics for the ADA Compliance Training 2024 program. It serves as the reference for all Accessibility Services Office (ASO) staff, school liaisons, and department heads involved in the delivery of accommodations (accoms) and compliance-related professional development for the fall semester. The plan was developed in consultation with the Office of Legal Affairs, Human Resources, and the District Safety Committee.

2. Program Overview
ADA Compliance Training 2024 (ACT2024) is the annual district-wide training initiative for all school-based staff who participate in the Section 504 and ADA accommodation process. The program includes a combination of mandatory core sessions, elective workshops, and a new asynchronous module designed to reduce scheduling conflicts for classroom teachers.

The program will run during the fall semester, with the main in-person sessions scheduled between early September and mid-November. The ADA Compliance Training 2024 planned_start_date is listed as 2024-09-03 in the training plan. Record status: historical. All sessions are planned to be held at the District Professional Development Center (PDC), Room 112, unless otherwise noted. A limited number of sessions will be offered at satellite locations to accommodate staff at the northern and southern school clusters.

3. Session Schedule
The following table lists all planned sessions for the fall term. Status is indicated as either Planned or Confirmed. Confirmed sessions have a reserved room and an assigned facilitator; Planned sessions are still awaiting room confirmation or facilitator assignment.

Note: The start date of the first session (ACT-101) aligns with the first day of the district’s fall professional development calendar. The date listed above was set during the spring planning cycle and has been confirmed by the PDC scheduling office.

4. Asynchronous Module
A new asynchronous module, ACT-AS1 (ADA Basics for Paraprofessionals), will be available starting 2024-09-03 via the district’s learning management system (LMS). This module is designed for paraprofessionals and instructional aides who support students with disabilities. The module takes approximately 90 minutes to complete and includes a short knowledge check at the end. Completion of ACT-AS1 is strongly encouraged for all paraprofessionals, though it is not a prerequisite for any in-person session.

5. Target Metrics

6. Assistive Technology Training Series (ATTS)

The Assistive Technology Training Series (ATTS) is a sub-track within the broader ACT2024 calendar, focused specifically on assistive technology tools and classroom implementation. ATTS sessions are open to all district staff but are recommended for special education teachers, paraprofessionals, and building-level technology coordinators. The series is designed to build practical skills in the tools most commonly requested through the accommodations (accoms) process.

**9. Evaluation and Quality Assurance**

**9.1 Overview**

The Accessibility Services Office will use a multi-method approach to evaluate the Fall 2024 training program. Evaluation will focus on three areas: participant learning, application of skills in the workplace, and overall program effectiveness. Results will be used to make real-time adjustments to sessions and to inform the Spring 2025 training cycle.

**9.2 Participant Feedback**

**9.2.1 Session Evaluation Forms**

A standardized session evaluation form will be distributed at the end of each session, both in print (for in-person sessions) and via the registration portal (for virtual sessions). The form will include:

- Overall satisfaction rating (1–5 scale)
- Relevance of content to daily responsibilities
- Quality of facilitation
- Adequacy of materials and handouts
- Open-ended questions for additional comments and suggestions

Participants will be asked to complete the form before leaving the session or within 24 hours for virtual sessions. The Accessibility Services Office will compile responses within five working days of each session.

**9.2.2 Mid-Program Pulse Check**

A brief mid-program survey will be sent to all Cohort A participants on 2024-10-18 and to all Cohort B participants on 2024-10-25. The pulse check will include five questions:

- Are the session topics meeting your expectations so far?
- Is the pace of the training appropriate?
- Do you have sufficient opportunities to practice new skills?
- What additional topics would you like covered in remaining sessions?
- Please share any logistical concerns (room, materials, timing).

Responses will be reviewed by the training coordinator within three working days. Common themes will be shared with facilitators before the next session.

**9.3 Knowledge Checks**

**9.3.1 Short Quizzes**

Each session will include a short, low-stakes quiz (5–8 questions) administered at the start of the following session. Quizzes will cover key concepts from the previous session. Quizzes will be scored and returned to participants within one week. Individual scores will be shared only with the participant; aggregate results will be shared with facilitators to identify topics that may need reinforcement.

**9.3.2 Pre- and Post-Training Assessment**

Participants will complete a pre-training assessment before the first session and a post-training assessment after the final session. The assessments will measure baseline and acquired knowledge across the core competency areas:

- Legal foundations (ADA, Section 504, and state requirements)
- Assistive technology basics
- Universal Design for Learning
- Document accessibility and remediation
- Communication and interaction with students with disabilities

Total participants enrolled in the Fall 2024 Accessibility Services Training: 35.
Participants who completed all required sessions (including make-up sessions where applicable): 32.
Participants who did not complete all requirements: 3.

Completion rate for the training period: 91.4%.
This rate reflects participants who met all attendance requirements and passed the associated knowledge checks. Participants with excused absences that did not require make-up are counted as complete only if they completed the knowledge check. Participants with unexcused absences who did not attend a make-up session are counted as not complete.

Average attendance across all scheduled sessions (Sessions 1–8): 94.6%.
